SI-4_title.answer: Developmental trajectories of neuroanatomical alterations associated with the 16p11.2 Copy Number Variations

NM2-1_modeling_methods.detail: Mixed-effects model with fixed effects for age (linear and quadratic), sex, and random effects for subject intercept and age slope. The model was fitted using the nlme package in R 3.4.0 to the NIHPD normative dataset to estimate developmental trajectories and compute Z-scores.
NM2-1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Mixed-effect models were used since it is appropriate to estimate growth in longitudinal studies that take repeated measures from the same individuals over time. ... The mixed-effects model that best fits the normative data is: Vol_i = β_0 + γ_0 + (β_1 + γ_1)(Age_i - 13) + β_2(Age_i - 13)² + β_3 Sex_i + ε_i ... The mixed-effect models were built using the nlme package.

NM2-2_response_variable.detail: Global volumes: total intracranial volume (TIV), global gray matter volume (GMV), white matter volume (WMV), lateral ventricle volume (CSF), and regional subcortical volumes (thalamus, putamen, caudate, globus pallidus). Voxel-level: Jacobian determinants from Tensor Based Morphometry (TBM) representing local volume differences, classified as deformation-derived morphometry (DDM).
NM2-2_response_variable.supporting_text: Whole-brain, individual lobes, thalamus, putamen, caudate, globus pallidus and ventricular volumes were calculated ... To investigate brain alterations beyond a priori specified anatomical regions of interest, we used Tensor Based Morphometry (TBM) ... The Jacobian determinant of the deformation field was computed for every voxel, log-transformed and used as a surrogate of the local volume difference between each subject and the ICBM152 template.

NM2-3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative model included age as a continuous variable (centered at 13 years), quadratic age term, and sex as fixed effects. Random effects included subject-specific intercept and age slope. Scanner effect was tested but not significant and excluded from the final model.
NM2-3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: we included both linear and quadratic effects of age in the fixed effects structure. Age was not divided into bins, but was considered as a continuous variable and was centered at 13 years - the mean age of NIHPD cohort. Linear effect of sex was also included in the fixed terms ... During model selection, a fixed effect for individual scanner was tested but found to be not significant and the model was associated with a higher Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC).
